claims: Setup now fails for any origin that isn't on github.com — scripts/bootstrap/codex-cloud-setup.sh:556-557 (and :179): `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner` fails when no remote is on a known GitHub host; because of `set -e`, setup aborts where it used to succeed
`verify_origin_write_access` pushes a branch to whatever origin is configured, running unconditionally even for non-GitHub origins that `verify_origin_git_auth` (line 158) deliberately skips
`gh repo view` with no argument doesn't necessarily pick `origin`: gh prefers a remote named `upstream` over `origin`, so it can probe the wrong repository

Every fresh container now triggers a Vercel deployment for the probe branch — scripts/bootstrap/codex-cloud-setup.sh:206, ui-dashboard/vercel.json:6-9: `vercel.json` only turns off deployments for `sentry-autofix/*`, so pushing `codex-cloud-write-probe-*` creates a deployment record and can do a full preview build of a branch deleted seconds later

The Playwright install now stops setup when it fails — codex-cloud-setup.sh:537, 583: unlike the deliberately non-fatal step in claude-code-web-setup.sh:141-153, it's on by default and a failure aborts setup before Envio codegen and the context check
That file's header comment ("this one additionally installs Playwright") is now out of date

The write probe has no opt-out: unlike Foundry, OSV, Trunk tools and Playwright there's no `CODEX_CLOUD_*=false` switch, so an environment with a deliberately read-only token can't run setup at all anymore

The docs' outbound-access list is incomplete — docs/notes/codex-cloud-setup.md:59-70: leaves out the distro apt mirrors (`archive.ubuntu.com` / `deb.debian.org`) used by the `gh` apt install and `playwright install --with-deps`

The API probe checks less than the docs say — codex-cloud-setup.sh:182-185, docs line 47: docs require pull-request read/write but only reads are checked; on a public repo those succeed with any valid token, so an under-scoped token for `gh pr create` still gets through

Tests only cover one failure path — codex-cloud-setup.test.sh:285-292: the "refused" case fails every `git` call, so only the create-failure path is exercised; the delete-failure path (line 217) has no test
The probe `git push` calls don't pass `--no-verify`: if setup runs where hooks are already configured (core.hooksPath, line 561), the Trunk pre-push hook runs against the probe push

judge_reasoning.3846756487: Review says the API probe only checks reads, while the docs claim PR read/write, so a token too narrow for gh pr create still passes.
judge_reasoning.3846756810: Review Problem 1: verify_origin_git_auth skips non-github.com origins, but the new gh repo view/api and write-push probes run unconditionally.
judge_reasoning.3846756918: Review only notes the delete-failure path has no test. It never says that setting created=false after a failed deletion stops the EXIT-trap cleanup.
judge_reasoning.3846756922: Review never raises that the timestamp plus $$ probe branch name may not be unique.
judge_reasoning.3846757143: Review Problem 2 flags the side effects of pushing a real probe branch on every setup run (Vercel deployments); same underlying issue, different fix than --dry-run.
judge_reasoning.3846757191: Review says the outbound-access list omits the distro apt mirrors needed by playwright install --with-deps and the gh apt install.

1.why: verify_github_api_capabilities (line 179) runs `gh repo view` without the non-GitHub-origin skip that verify_origin_git_auth has at lines 158-161; this is the known 179 [P2] consistency item.

2.why: verify_origin_write_access is called right after verify_origin_git_auth (lines 556-557) and also lacks its non-GitHub skip. It's the same inconsistency the known 179 item describes.

3.why: Line 179 calls `gh repo view` with no repo argument. gh picks the base repo from its remotes with `upstream` ranked ahead of `origin`, so the API probes can hit a different repo than the one the git push probe uses (origin).

4.why: ui-dashboard/vercel.json turns off deployments only for `sentry-autofix/*`. Pushing `codex-cloud-write-probe-*` therefore creates a Vercel deployment, and vercel-ignore-build.sh only skips the build when HEAD has no dashboard changes versus main.

5.why: Accurate, but a design choice: the docs say setup fails closed on tool-install failure, list cdn.playwright.dev as required, and offer the CODEX_CLOUD_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT_DEPS=false opt-out.

6.why: The header of claude-code-web-setup.sh (lines 9-10) still says 'this one additionally installs Playwright', but codex-cloud-setup.sh now installs it too; the diff left the comment unchanged.

7.why: True that there's no switch, but blocking read-only tokens is the stated purpose ('fails early when a token can fetch but cannot publish'). This is a preference, not a defect.

8.why: Same as the known docs:70 item 'Document the distribution package source.'

9.why: Lines 182-185 only GET `pulls`, so pull-request write access is never checked. This is the known 195 items.

10.why: In the test file, the refused case makes every git call return 1, so it stops at the create step. No test covers create succeeding and delete failing, which is where the known cleanup bug lives.

11.why: Setup runs on a fresh container and only sets core.hooksPath at line 561, after the probe (lines 556-557), so no Trunk pre-push hook is active during the probe pushes.
